maya (sec): Heads-up — we have a scheduled cert/key rotation for the control-plane API tomorrow 09:30 PT. Quick clarifying Qs before we flip: who will be the writable owner of the KMS key alias during the rollout, and what handshake/log fields should we redact from debug logs? cc @raj (infra) @julie (oncall)

raj (infra): Owner will be infra oncall by default. We'll hand off temporary IAM to the release lead for <2h window. KMS alias: projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/ctl-plane/cryptoKeys/ctl-rot-v3.

julie (oncall): noted — I'll be the release lead for the window. Requesting the IAM change now via the approvals queue. Can someone confirm exactly which perms we need?

praveen (eng-runtime): For the rotation we need: 
- kms.cryptoKeyVersions.useToDecrypt (for fetching private key material)
- kms.cryptoKeyVersions.viewOnKey (for metadata)
- compute.instances.get if we need to signal instances (we usually restart via service orchestrator so not required)
Keep access scoped to the alias and set expiration TTL.

maya (sec): For logs: redact client IPs and raw TLS ClientHello/ServerHello payloads. It's fine to keep handshake outcome (success/failure) + ciphersuite name. Do NOT persist full cert chain blobs in plain logs. Also add an annotation field "rotation_id" instead of dumping keys.

raj (infra): Got it. We'll patch the log filter to mask these fields and run a dry-run against staging. Quick test commands: 
```
# verify cert chain and server response
openssl s_client -connect api.control.redwood.internal:443 -servername api.control.redwood.internal -showcerts
# quick TLS handshake summary
openssl s_client -connect api.control.redwood.internal:443 -cipher 'TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384:TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256' </dev/null
```

julie (oncall): For post-rotation checks, can we add a smoke check step to the runbook to hit /health and run an end-to-end signed request (token + client cert) to ensure mutual auth paths good?

praveen (eng-runtime): Yes — add: 1) curl with token header 2) a short script that establishes tls connection and validates server cert matches pinned fingerprint. Example: 
```
python -c "import ssl,socket,hashlib; s=ssl.create_default_context(); conn=s.wrap_socket(socket.socket(), server_hostname='api.control.redwood.internal'); conn.connect(('api.control.redwood.internal',443)); d=conn.getpeercert(True); print(hashlib.sha256(d).hexdigest())"
```

maya (sec): Approvals nit: for any IAM elevation, capture a single approval message in the thread (who approved + expiry). We should also attach the runbook PR link. I'll pre-approve the request once IAM request has the expiry TTL.

raj (infra): I've created the PR to update the runbook and log filters: https://git.internal.redwood/runbooks/ctl-rotation/pull/142 — includes redaction rules and step-by-step. Requesting one more reviewer from security.

kms-bot: Access grant event queued: request-id=rg-20260317-88, expires-in=2h, requested-by=julie.

julie (oncall): Approved. I confirm temporary IAM will expire at 11:40 PT. Will post final verification output here after rotation. :thumbsup:

praveen (eng-runtime): Small heads-up — some legacy clients in EU region still negotiate TLS1.2 with AES-GCM only. We should keep TLS1.2 enabled but disallow old CBC ciphers. Will add that note to PR.

maya (sec): Good catch. Make sure we log a metric for any TLS version downgrade attempts during the rollout window so we can alert if unexpected clients pop up.

julie (oncall): Rotation done. Verifications: /health 200, smoke signed request OK, pinned cert fingerprint matched. Post-rollout logs show handshake_success with cipher TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256, and 3 TLS1.2 connections (expected). No sensitive blobs in logs. Closing ticket.

maya (sec): Thanks all. Please keep the PR merged and the runbook entry pinned to the incident for 30d. I'll open a quick follow-up to formalize the log redaction pattern across other control-plane services.

raj (infra): Thanks team.
